recentItems.title: King George Hero Banbridge Wins on the Flat at Gowran | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
King George VI Chase-winner Banbridge (4/1) proved a surprise star turn on the Flat at Gowran Park in September 2026, merrily landing the concluding Racing Again September 19th Maiden on his first start on the Flat at the age of 10.

Winner of both the Punchestown Champion Chase and King George in 2024, Banbridge had previously unseated rider in April's Grand National, and was using today's reappearance as a prep run for the American Grand National at Far Hills on October 17.

Racing behind the leaders, strong-travelling Bandridge swept aside his rivals over a furlong out and was an eased-down winner under jockey Joey Sheridan, beating Ballybawn Belter by two lengths.

Regarding the Ronnie Bartlett-owned gelding, winning trainer Joseph O'Brien, earlier successful with the Sheridan-partnered Starborn Legend , said “We didn't expect him to win, but thought it'd be a nice place for him to get the season off to a start. He really went through the race with great enthusiasm and he won snug.

#horseracing #gowranpark

recentItems.title: The Verdict: Horses To Follow From The Curragh, Sandown & Goodwood | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Angus McNae and Josh Kerr analyse the week's action through the RaceIQ sectional data, from the Curragh, Sandown Park and Goodwood — and get to grips with softer ground.

Kokbastu is the horse of the week. Winning his third on the bounce at Sandown off the best time index of the day.

At the Curragh, Darkness Falls quickened clear for Aidan O'Brien and Ryan Moore, the only runner in the race to hit 40mph, while Push The Boat Out found a remarkable turn of foot to beat Great Barrier Reef.

Zavateri won the Celebration Mile at Goodwood, Alfred Wallace took a Solario the data doesn't rate highly, and Light Of Dawn came out on top of a race full of trouble in running, with Eabha arguably the unlucky one.

#horseracing #theverdict

recentItems.title: Group Three honours for Light Of Dawn, James Doyle, Karl Burke and Wathnan Racing! #horseracing
LIGHT OF DAWN lands 2026 Prestige Fillies' Stakes at Goodwood for re-routed James Doyle | Full Race
recentItems.description:
James Doyle may have missed a Group winner in France when his flight to Deauville failed to take off but he parachuted in to Goodwood to pick up a valuable consolation prize in the 2026 Virgin Bet Prestige Fillies’ Stakes aboard Light Of Dawn.

Wathnan’s retained jockey had been due to fly to Normandy to partner Hamad Al Jehani’s Diego Ventura, winner of the Group Three Barriere Prix Quincey, only to be grounded at Duxford Airfield.

But after rerouting to the Sussex Downs, Doyle replaced Clifford Lee on the Showcasing filly and powered to a convincing success, landing the Group Three prize on the 4-1 shot by a length and a quarter from Eabha with the John and Thady Gosden-trained Baaeed filly Coaxed back in third.

“We got to the plane to go to Deauville but that didn’t take off but the plane to Goodwood was there so I switched over and I was quite lucky in that regard,” Doyle told Racing TV. “Obviously I’m delighted to get on her and I was very pleased with her."

#horseracing #goodwood

recentItems.title: JM Jungle toughs it out to take the 2026 Beverley Bullet | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Jm Jungle got up in the dying strides to claim the 2026 William Hill Beverley Bullet Sprint.

A Group Two winner last season and sent off the 7-4 favourite, class told in a thrilling finish on the Westwood as the six-year-old finally got his nose in front after giving a good account of himself in high-ranking contests once again this season.

The John and Sean Quinn-trained gelding was only beaten two and three-quarter lengths in the Nunthorpe at York last week and quickly returned to action got a deserved first victory of the season in East Yorkshire.

Five of the eight runners were still in with a chance as they entered the final furlong with Tim Easterby’s Argentine Tango holding the advantage on the rail as they entered the last 100 yards and Jm Jungle pursuing down the centre of the course.

Jm Jungle responded to the urgings of regular pilot Jason Hart, reeling in Argentine Tango before asserting close home to register a half length success. Badri was a neck further adrift in third and course specialist Elegant Erin a short head off that rival in fourth.

John Quinn said: “He’s done that really well and he’s been running really well all year in Group Ones so he deserved it.

“He ran well in the Nunthorpe, he ran well at Royal Ascot, he ran well at Goodwood and he just got his head in front today.

“He’s in the Flying Five at the Curragh in two weeks so he might go there.”

#horseracing #beverley

recentItems.title: BetMGM Solario Stakes: Alfred Wallace joins rich roll of honour | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Alfred Wallace put his experience to good use when running out a narrow winner of the BetMGM Solario Stakes at Sandown.

Ed Walker’s two-year-old was making his seventh appearance of the season in a Group Three contest that had a notable late absentee in hot favourite Rock Montreal, who was taken out on account of the deteriorating conditions.

Alfred Wallace had impressed when winning the Listed Pat Eddery Stakes at Ascot last month and having since finished fourth in Acomb Stakes at York, he was an 11-4 shot to get back on the winning trail at Group Three level just 10 days later.

Kieran Shoemark kept things simple on the chestnut son of Dubawi, positioning him on the heels of the pacesetting Sonic Angel before taking over and committing for home two furlongs from the finish.

While some of his less experienced rivals took a while to find their stride and wandered when coming under pressure, Alfred Wallace stayed straight and true and had enough up his sleeve to see off Dover Street by half a length, with Breacher the same distance further behind in third.

Walker said: “What a dude, he’s an absolute star to back up 10 days after York.

“I was really cross when I saw the entries for this as the plan was always to come straight here, but I got tempted by York and probably didn’t give Aidan’s horse (Haffner) the respect he deserved.

“When I saw the entries for this I had to put him in and spent my week kicking myself for going to York, but what a tough little horse – he helped me out of trouble.”

The Lambourn handler plans to give Alfred Wallace a shot at Group One glory before the season is out, adding: “You can’t see a rib on him, he’s been busy and never leaves an oat. He’s always fresh as paint at home and he’s got such a great appetite for it.

“A few high-profile non-runners probably helped us there but I see William Muir every morning and he thinks the world of his horse who was third (Breacher).

“Our fellow just has that battle-hardened experience, he’s small and strong and tough. I’ve not trained many Dubawis and people always mention their constitution and that is what this fellow has.

“He’s got his Listed and Group Three wins now and that is massively important to owners Rockcliffe Stud.

“I think by the law of physics he will find life tougher next year when the more backward horses are coming out and that is why we are squeezing the lemon a little bit this year.

“We’ll definitely have a shot at a Group One with him, he’s in everything and I’ll just have to try not to run him in all of them!”

#horseracing

recentItems.title: Nina Carberry rolls back the years with emotional charity win | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Like old times!

MEP Nina Carberry enjoyed a 17-year career as a rider and rode the likes of Gold Cup winner Don Cossack in his formative years as well as winning races such as the Irish Grand National.

Teaming up with old ally Gordon Elliott, Carberry partnered Ndaawi to success in the Pat Smullen Cancer Trials Ireland Charity Race at the Curragh in a feelgood story supporting Ireland's biggest charity raceday which has raised over €1.2m for a wonderful cause in honour of the multiple champion jockey who we sadly lost back in September 2020 at the age of 43.

recentItems.title: Zavateri set for Champions Day after Celebration Mile romp | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Eve Johnson Houghton was thrilled to see her stable star Zavateri stamp his class on the Virgin Bet Celebration Mile at Goodwood.

A Group One-winning juvenile in last season’s National Stakes, the Without Parole colt had endured a frustrating three-year-old campaign so far, with an early-season setback ruling him out of a potential Classic bid.

He performed creditably to finish fifth in both Goodwood’s Sussex Stakes last month and the City of York Stakes on the Knavesmire just last week, and he was the 11-10 favourite to strike Group Two gold seven days later.

After being settled in midfield by Charlie Bishop, Zavateri quickened up smartly in the rain-softened ground to claim the lead with a furlong still to run and the further he went the better he looked, eventually passing the post with three-and-a-half lengths in hand over Qirat.

“On hearing the ground was heavy I said to Charlie ‘are we going to run’ and he said, ‘let’s see’. I said if he goes on the ground he would win and he did,” said Johnson Houghton.

“He is from very small beginnings but has developed into a machine, and he showed the turn of foot I knew he had.”

Zavateri is set for an immediate jump to the highest level, with the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes on Champions Day at Ascot (October 17) uppermost in his trainer’s mind.

She added: “Now he will go the the QEII, end of conversation. We need to go back to Group One company at Ascot I’m really keen to do that.

“We (father Fulke Johnson Houghton) won it twice with Rose Bowl a long time ago (1975 and 1976) and it’s the right race for this horse.”
